Ahava
uh-HAY-vuh
proper noun / place
From Hebrew ʾAhăwā, a river (or canal) district where Ezra proclaimed a fast before the return caravan entered the dangerous road (Ezr 8:15, 21, 31).

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Ahava is the river-camp where Ezra assembled returning exiles, found no Levites at first, then proclaimed a fast that they might afflict themselves before God to seek of Him a right way for themselves, their little ones, and their substance (Ezr 8:15, 21). Ezra was ashamed to ask a band of soldiers of the king, because he had told the king that the hand of God is upon all them for good that seek Him. At Ahava they fasted and besought God, and He was intreated of them; later they departed from the river of Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month (Ezr 8:31). Ahava is therefore the school of dependent courage. Faith does not deny danger; it refuses to make unbelief’s request after a public confession of God’s hand. The modern church often wants either armed presumption or prayerless planning. Ezra gives fasting, little ones, substance, and a road under the hand of God. Hold Ahava, and hold the doctrine that seeking the Lord is the first logistics of any holy journey home to Zion under hostile powers.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

River-camp of Ezra’s caravan; place of fasting for a right way without a royal escort.

expand to see more

AHAVA, a river (or canal) where Ezra camped the return caravan.

There he proclaimed a fast to seek a right way of the Lord.

He was ashamed to request soldiers after confessing God’s hand.

God was intreated of them at Ahava.

They departed from the river of Ahava toward Jerusalem.

📖 Key Scripture

Ezr 8:21 — "Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God, to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance."

Ezr 8:22 — "For I was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way: because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him."

Ezr 8:23 — "So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us."

Ezr 8:31 — "Then we departed from the river of Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go unto Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy, and of such as lay in wait by the way."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Ahava is reduced to travel diary; it is fasting logistics under a public confession of God’s hand.

expand to see more

The corruption is to treat Ezra’s fast as optional spirituality bolted onto planning. Ahava is where planning was fasting. Recover dependent courage that matches words spoken before kings.

A second misuse is prosperity presumption: if God’s hand is good, no danger exists. Ezra names enemies and ambush while trusting deliverance. Recover sober faith, not swagger.

Ahava is Ezra’s river-camp of fasting before the unescorted road to Jerusalem.

Usage

"They departed from the river of Ahava toward Jerusalem."

"Ahava is the camp of dependent courage."
